label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
**★★★★☆**

Moved with Kilbarrack Van Co on Saturday 17th October, Phibsborough to Drumcondra. Two bed flat but it was mostly my stuff, so a fair bit but not a full family house. The new place is a 4th floor walk-up with no lift, which I was dreading. Going with 4 stars, and here's why, for anyone trying to decide.

**Booking and price**

Booked through their website and paid a €50 deposit by Revolut, all handy. The quote was €340 for up to 4 hours with two lads and the van. Every other quote I got was €450 or more, so they were the best value by a good bit. It took about three and a half hours in the end, so no going over.

**The not so good**

They were meant to arrive at 9 and turned up at half 10. In fairness I got a text at 8:40 saying the previous job had overrun, so I wasn't left wondering. Still, I spent an hour and a half sitting on boxes with a cold coffee. For me it wasn't the end of the world, but if you're on a tight handover with a landlord or have to be out of your old place by a set time, it would be. I'd mention any hard deadline when you book, and maybe ask to be the first job of the day.

The other thing was my brass floor lamp. Everything else got wrapped in blankets but the lamp didn't, and the base got chipped on the way. It was my nanny's lamp, so I was a bit gutted. It still works and it's not a disaster, but if you've anything like that, point it out at the start and make sure it gets wrapped. Lads, wrap the lamps!

**The good**

Once they got going they were brilliant. The couch wouldn't go round the turn on the 3rd floor and I thought we'd be stuck. One of the lads (Kev I think) just took the legs off with an allen key he had in his pocket and it went straight in. No fuss, no swearing at the stairs, no taking chunks out of the walls. Four floors with no lift is a lot and they never once complained.

They also put the bed back together for me without being asked, which was class because the last thing you want after a move is building a bed at 10 at night. And they took away a flat pack shelf I didn't want, which saved me a trip to the dump.

Dessie knocked €40 off the bill afterwards because of the lateness. I didn't even ask him to. That says a lot about how he runs things.

**Would I use them again?**

Yes, honestly. For the price they're very hard to beat, and the lads were sound, careful with the furniture and good at problem solving on awkward stairs. The two things I'd change are the timing and wrapping the fragile bits. If you're flexible on the time and you flag anything delicate, I'd recommend them.

**Tips if you're booking:**
- Tell them about any deadline (key handover etc.) up front
- Point out lamps, mirrors or anything sentimental and ask for it to be wrapped
- Mention stairs and no lift when getting the quote so they can plan for it
- Have an allen key handy anyway, though Kev seems to carry his own

Thanks Dessie and the lads. Next time just wrap the lamp 😄

---

That comes to roughly 560 words. I wasn't sure about Kev's name, so I left it as "Kev I think," which sounds natural in a review. If you want to drop the bit about asking for the first job of the day so it's less pointed, it'll still read fine without it.
